subject: Business
title: Cloud Computing: From Owning to Renting
description: A short lesson to help you apply Cloud Computing: From Owning to Renting.

hook.text: In 2006, a startup needed $100,000 for servers. Today, they need a credit card and AWS. The barrier to entry vanished.

buildup.text: Cloud computing lets businesses rent computing power on-demand instead of buying and maintaining their own servers.

discovery.text: AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud rent servers by the second. Scale up for Black Friday, scale down on Tuesday.

twist.text: Amazon built AWS for internal needs. Then realized they could sell spare capacity.

climax.text: The cloud enabled Netflix, Spotify, Slack, and Zoom — companies that couldn't exist without elastic, pay-as-you-go compute.

punchline.text: Someone else's computer became the foundation of the modern economy.

quiz.question: Why was AWS originally created?
options: Amazon built it for internal needs and then sold spare capacity externally
It was designed from the start as a public service
A government grant funded its development

details.summary: Cloud computing shifted IT from owning expensive servers to renting computing power on demand from providers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. This model lets startups access enterprise-grade infrastructure without upfront capital, fundamentally lowering barriers to innovation.
details.whyItMatters: Cloud computing democratized access to computing power, enabling a startup in a garage to use the same infrastructure as a Fortune 500 company. It is the invisible foundation upon which most modern digital businesses are built.
takeaways: Cloud computing rents computing resources instead of owning physical servers
AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud dominate the infrastructure-as-a-service market
Pay-per-use pricing eliminates massive upfront capital requirements

faq.question: How did cloud computing change the economics of starting a company?
faq.answer: Before cloud, startups needed tens of thousands for servers before writing a line of code. Cloud computing lets founders start with a few dollars per month and scale only when customer demand justifies it. This dramatically reduced the capital needed to test and launch new ideas.

faq.question: What are the risks of depending on cloud providers?
faq.answer: Vendor lock-in makes switching providers expensive and complex. Outages at major providers can take down thousands of dependent businesses simultaneously. Data sovereignty concerns arise when information is stored across jurisdictions with different privacy laws.
